sites.name: Athabasca Valles
sites.description: Athabasca Valles, young flood channels with lava-covered plains.

sources.dataset: megt44n090hb.img
USGS SIM 3292 Global Geologic Map of Mars (Tanaka et al., 2014)
Published orbital spectral and geological studies of Athabasca Valles
MGS TES dayside thermal inertia (Putzig & Mellon 2007)
OMEGA/MEx NIR albedo (Ody et al. 2012), 1.08 um
MACDA v2.0

context.note: Context only; not used in the similarity score (no matching Earth values yet).

limitations: Regional and detailed MOLA terrain have approximately 460 m pixel resolution; the detailed footprint is not 30 m terrain.
Global USGS geological mapping (1:20,000,000) cannot resolve individual flood-lava flows and channel deposits within a 5 km site.
Mineral detections from Athabasca Valles literature are tentative and regional; no individual mineral is confirmed in the selected 5 km footprint, and no mineral-area fraction is mapped.
MGS/TES thermal inertia is coarse and needs a comparable Earth-side product before similarity scoring.
OMEGA near-infrared 1.08 micrometre albedo cannot be directly scored against Earth's broadband albedo.
MACDA wind and pressure are modeled atmospheric context, never part of Earth similarity scores.
Atmospheric reference coordinates are 91.01 km from Athabasca terrain center; they are not confirmed model cell coordinates.

USGS SIM 3292 Global Geologic Map of Mars (Tanaka et al., 2014)
Seelos et al. (2014), Mineralogy of the MSL Curiosity landing site in Gale crater as observed by MRO/CRISM
MGS TES dayside thermal inertia (Putzig & Mellon 2007)
OMEGA/MEx NIR albedo (Ody et al. 2012), 1.08 um
MACDA v2.0

context.note: Context only; not used in the similarity score (no matching Earth values yet).

limitations: Geology is based on a coarse 1:20,000,000 global map, unlike Jezero's local geologic map.
Minerals come from qualitative literature observations; no measured 5 km mineral area fractions exist.
Wind and pressure are regional MACDA modeled context, not local in-situ measurements.
OMEGA NIR albedo is not directly comparable to Earth broadband albedo.

Thermal inertia and albedo values are real Gale-region measurements centered roughly 52 km from Bradbury Landing. These should be displayed with their source locations and not scored as local 5 km surface similarity without recalculation.

context.geology_dominant_unit: Hesperian and Noachian highland undivided unit
context.note: Context only; not used in the similarity score (no matching Earth values yet).

limitations: Both 10 km and 5 km terrain footprints use native MOLA ~460 m resolution, insufficient to resolve Victoria Crater's ~800 m rim and walls. The downloaded HiRISE DTM was not used because it did not cover the full 5 km square.
Global USGS geological mapping (1:20,000,000) cannot resolve Victoria Crater's local Burns formation strata and rim deposits within the 5 km footprint.
Opportunity's in-situ Victoria Crater mineral detections and CRISM interpretations are point/outcrop-scale, not quantitative mineral-area maps for the whole 5 km square.
MGS/TES thermal inertia is coarse and needs a comparable Earth-side product before similarity scoring.
OMEGA near-infrared 1.08 micrometre albedo cannot be directly scored against Earth's broadband albedo.
MACDA wind and pressure are modeled atmospheric context, never part of Earth similarity scores.
Atmospheric reference coordinates are 2.96 km from Victoria terrain center; they are not confirmed model cell coordinates.
